title: fix(anthropic): finish Opus 5.5 defaults and thinking display
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Follow-up to #155966: core Opus 5.5 support is already landed, but rolling defaults still select Opus 5 and Anthropic transports do not consistently forward thinking-display preferences. CLI setup must preserve authored model selections rather than reinterpret them as the new rolling default.

## User Impact

- Bare `opus` and new Anthropic API/CLI onboarding and media defaults select Opus 5.5. Explicit Opus 5 IDs, versioned aliases, and authored alias targets remain pinned.
- Primary/fallback alias selections survive interactive and noninteractive CLI setup, including auth-profile suffixes and legacy/canonical row collisions.
- `thinkingDisplay` reaches native and simple Anthropic transports; mandatory-thinking normalization remains with its existing owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

The merged foundation supplies the model contract, catalog, and replay policy. This follow-up completes defaults and display forwarding. CLI migration consults the existing configured-alias resolver before built-in aliases and resolves Anthropic targets before migrating legacy rows, preserving canonical metadata and other-provider aliases. No public SDK expansion or new configuration setting.

## Evidence

- **Live proof passed on production-identical commit:** `34e515851017f0b100db8be415722f99448fd36c`, [Blacksmith Testbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35820014547), wrapper and launcher **exit 0**. Final head `955a484ebd08b39ef6cd9e572976e7ad5d0f180c` differs from that live-tested commit only in the two audited pricing/PDF test files; no production code changed. Nine HTTP 200 requests served the exact model; five runtime calls included **four signed-thinking replays and zero thinking drops**, real read-tool continuations, and three persisted turns. Medium default, saved-off→adaptive/low, and omitted display through both adapters were verified without rewriting requests. Isolated home removal and lease release were verified.
- **Focused tests:** 33 CLI setup tests (29.07s Vitest / 30.54s wrapper); 19 QA flow tests (8.22s / 9.47s); 11 pricing and 12 PDF cases (0.754s and 5.46s Vitest; 7.92s grouped wrapper). Earlier unchanged-owner evidence remains 450 tests across 12 files / 72.37s.
- **Checks/build:** changed production/test checks pass, including types, lint, guards, six doctor tests and zero runtime cycles. Full build passed in **5m7.4s**; subsequent commits change tests only, so the production build remains applicable.
- **Review/audit:** independent P2 reviews are scoped-clean after addressing the authored-alias and legacy-row collision findings. Complete audits cover **16 changed test/support files**. No skipped tests or claimed overall CI speed savings.
- **Landing status:** [Final CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35821757439) passed on `955a484ebd08b39ef6cd9e572976e7ad5d0f180c`; fresh readback shows 172 successful, 36 skipped, one neutral, and no failing/pending checks. Native merge admission remains authoritative. The live proof covers API/embedded runtime, **not native Claude CLI login E2E**; registered CLI setup tests stub auth availability while exercising real migration and result projection.

<details>
<summary>Regression controls, test audit, and fixture limitations</summary>

The original alias regression failed through both registered setup paths; an independently identified legacy/canonical collision also failed before repair. The CLI file replaces a builder-versus-entrypoint self-comparison with three independently asserted cases (31→33), preserving distinct security, error, auth, routing and migration coverage. Removing a Record cast allowed an exact shrink-only assertion baseline update.

CI run 35818900153/job 107046529067 found one stale QA default expectation, with 1,326 other cases passing. Its correction independently expects rolling Opus 5.5 and retains explicit Opus 5 coverage. The full-file audit removed a resolver-to-itself oracle and unused fixture, and replaced a real 20ms wait—which could not exceed the 5ms+5s watchdog—with deterministic fake-clock coverage beyond that grace. All 19 cases remain; timers are restored and checked for leaks. The remaining CI failures were stale canonical-Opus pricing and automatic PDF-default fixtures. Their full-file repairs retain explicit Opus 5 pins, check frozen numeric pricing rather than object identity, consolidate four repeated MiniMax fixtures, and remove an unnecessary heavyweight test-helper import. Pricing cases are 10→11; PDF cases remain 12. Fresh P2 review is scoped-clean.

Final hosted CI job wall times: QA shard 227s, compact-small-8 (including PDF) 401s, compact-small-10 (including pricing) 162s. These are multi-file/job totals including setup, not per-file incremental cost or claimed savings.

The bounded local original-shard replay reproduced that target failure but also encountered unchanged QA-bus malformed-JSON/process fixture timeouts. Their local cause remains unresolved; that entire local replay is not claimed passing. The original hosted shard passed its other 76 files.

Initial standalone live fixtures lacked the command/reply layer’s reusable skill snapshot, genuinely changing the system prefix and triggering the intended drop-block recovery. The final fixture uses that existing lifecycle and canonical CLI resource cleanup/one-shot finalization. Optional memory-worker loading warnings occurred; this is not a memory E2E claim. Earlier incomplete probe processes were stopped and their owned Testboxes verified completed. The final lease was `tbx_01m369myxp3xsbj5yqq1jm016s`; command time was 183.704s. Testbox’s Actions lease workflow may show cancellation on release; the wrapper’s terminal exit and inspected artifacts are the proof receipt.

</details>

Thanks @fuller-stack-dev for the reproduction, live verification request, and test-audit direction.
